title: At the table
subtitle: Serving and pairing Meunier
objectives: Know how long to keep it

steps.title: Fruity bubbles
steps.body: Meunier-rich Champagnes suit food well: charcuterie, roast chicken, salmon, gougères and mild cheeses. Their red fruit and roundness handle slightly richer dishes than lean Blanc de Blancs. Still Meunier, like Coteaux Champenois rouge, suits light meats.

steps.title: Service and age
steps.body: Serve Champagne at 8 to 10 degrees, in a white wine glass rather than a narrow flute to let its aromas show. Meunier-led Champagnes are often best within a few years of release, though top ones from old vines age well.
steps.highlight: 8 to 10 degrees, in a wine glass

steps.prompt: Why might a white wine glass be better than a flute for Meunier Champagne?
steps.explanation: A wider bowl lets aromas gather.

steps.body: Gougères, little cheese puffs from Burgundy, are a classic Champagne snack. Their richness suits a fruity, Meunier-led Champagne.

steps.prompt: Meunier-led Champagnes are generally drunk younger than Chardonnay-led ones.
steps.explanation: Yes. Meunier matures faster, though top examples can age.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Meunier Champagne suits gougères, salmon and chicken
Serve at 8 to 10 degrees, in a wine glass
Most are best within a few years
